destruction_assays.test: Can a discrete 2-node feedback loop x_{t+1} = f(y_t), y_{t+1} = g(x_t) explain all observed dynamics?
destruction_assays.result: YES. The system decomposes into an ordinary discrete dynamical system over the product state space X x Y.

destruction_assays.test: Can categorical adjunctions (F -| G) or typed bisimulation games model the reciprocal interaction?
destruction_assays.result: YES. In category theory, an adjunction between the category of Rules and the category of Rulefields models the exact bidirectional relationship without postulating an ad-hoc primitive.

destruction_assays.test: Does unrolling the reciprocal interaction into a finite feedforward DAG of depth k reproduce all outputs for any finite budget?
destruction_assays.result: YES. For any finite compute budget T, the unrolled DAG is observationally identical to the feedback loop.

destruction_assays.test: Is there any empirical observation from independent physical acquisition backing RRR?
destruction_assays.result: NO. All evidence originates from internal synthetic simulations. Physical acquisition credit = 0.

destruction_assays.test: Does instantaneous reciprocity (t = t) violate causal order?
destruction_assays.result: YES. Instantaneous loops without time delay produce algebraic circularity or deadlock. When time delay dt > 0 is introduced, the system becomes an ordinary causal sequence.

destruction_assays.test: Does a standard stateful coroutine with typed interfaces require fewer assumptions?
destruction_assays.result: YES. Standard coroutines require zero ontological additions and explain all observed data.

destruction_assays.test: Does perceived emergence depend on the observer lacking access to intermediate feedback states?
destruction_assays.result: YES. When intermediate states are hidden by coarse-graining, the output appears as "instantaneous emergence". When observed at full fidelity, it is step-by-step computation.
